findings: S3 put/get command construction validates provider-neutral requests and rejects provider-bucket drift before emitting commands or receipts.
Targeted unit tests cover S3 put/get command shapes, provider receipts, provider-bucket drift, and adapter config validation alongside OCI/domain regression tests.
S3-specific endpoint, region, bucket, and object-path behavior lives only in the adapter crate; domain owns the inward-facing object provider port contract.
StorageProviderKind gained an additive S3ObjectStorage variant; existing object/block port request and receipt shapes remain unchanged.
No external SDK dependency added; deterministic S3 command structs follow the existing OCI adapter lint/test pattern.
S3 receipts carry provider_request_id and provider_evidence_ref for audit-chain correlation without raw object bytes.
Adapter command bodies carry object_body_ref/result_body_ref plus KMS/ciphertext refs, not raw object payload bytes or AWS credentials.
Request translation is deterministic string assembly with no network call or allocation-heavy abstraction beyond canonical command construction.
The new second provider reuses the existing provider-neutral object port instead of introducing provider-specific branches in domain/API crates.
ChangeSet is isolated to one new adapter crate, one provider enum addition, catalog row, plan status, and evidence.
